scenario: AITA for not being emotional on my wedding day? | My wife and I didn’t do many traditional things for our wedding. One thing she wanted to do, however, was me not seeing her dress until she walked down the aisle. I agreed. She kept saying I’d love it, she loved it. She and her best friend (maid of honor) kept sharing reaction posts of grooms happy crying upon getting a first look at their bride, tagging me in it, saying “this will be you!” Day of, wife walks down. She herself did look beautiful, as always. However, I was not big on the dress. To me, it wasn’t at all flattering. But I didn’t focus on that. I focused on her. I smiled. I didn’t break down in tears like some reaction pics/videos. The maid of honor kept nudging me until I looked at her and mouthed “stop”. We got married, kissed, the whole thing. Everything was fine at the reception. Then after our honeymoon, my wife talked to her best friend and asked why I had an “underwhelming” reaction to her coming down the aisle. I said I didn’t. She said there are pictures that guests took and I don’t look how she pictured. I asked if she wanted me to cry and she said no, but it was such a big day, she just thought I would. I said I was estatic to marry her and that showed, without me being over dramatic. I also said I had her friend nudging me the whole time and that was unfair to me. Finally I asked if we had a wedding or a play, because I never got lines. Now she’s mad at me. Am I an ass here? I do feel bad she’s disappointed but I couldn’t force myself to have a reaction.

Everything was fine at the reception. Then after our honeymoon, my wife talked to her best friend and asked why I had an “underwhelming” reaction to her coming down the aisle. I said I didn’t. She said there are pictures that guests took and I don’t look how she pictured. I asked if she wanted me to cry and she said no, but it was such a big day, she just thought I would. I said I was estatic to marry her and that showed, without me being over dramatic. I also said I had her friend nudging me the whole time and that was unfair to me. Finally I asked if we had a wedding or a play, because I never got lines. Now she’s mad at me. Am I an ass here? I do feel bad she’s disappointed but I couldn’t force myself to have a reaction.

prediction.raw: Based on the scenario, I would say that you are not the asshole (NTA). Here's why: 1. **You agreed to the surprise**: You agreed to not see your wife's dress until she walked down the aisle, which was her idea. You didn't have any control over the situation, and you went along with it. 2. **You focused on her, not the dress**: You chose to focus on your wife's beauty and happiness, rather than the dress itself. This shows that you were present and engaged with her, even if you didn't have a dramatic reaction. 3. **You didn't promise to cry**: You didn't promise your wife that you would cry or have a specific reaction. You simply agreed to go along with the surprise. 4. **You were honest with your wife**: When your wife asked you about your reaction, you were honest with her. You explained that you were ecstatic to marry her, but you didn't feel the need to be dramatic. 5. **You called out the maid of honor**: You pointed out that the maid of honor was nudging you to react, which was unfair to you. This shows that you're not afraid to speak up and stand up for yourself. It's understandable that your wife might have been disappointed by your reaction, but it's not your fault that you didn't meet her expectations. You were true to yourself and your feelings, and that's what matters most in a marriage.
